title: LS-MDRM Claim Status Ontology
description: Defines valid epistemic statuses, transition rules, EPR computation, and promotion-detection requirements.

OBSERVED.definition: The proposition is directly supported by recorded, bound evidence without additional inference.
OBSERVED.example: HTTP 410 was returned by both repetition runs.
OBSERVED.promotion_notes: OBSERVED is not a promotion target from any weaker status; it requires fresh evidence binding, not re-labeling.

DERIVED.definition: The proposition follows from one or more OBSERVED propositions through a stated transformation rule.
DERIVED.example: The platform is retired (derived from HTTP 410 + retirement notice + chronology).
DERIVED.promotion_notes: Derivation requires an explicit transformation rule. Implicit derivation is not licensed.

HYPOTHESIZED.definition: The proposition is a candidate explanation or prediction not yet supported by direct evidence.
HYPOTHESIZED.example: A migration to an equivalent receiver would preserve experimental comparability.
HYPOTHESIZED.promotion_notes: Hypotheses require operationalization before promotion to OBSERVED or DERIVED.

COUNTERFACTUAL.definition: The proposition describes what would have occurred under conditions that did not obtain.
COUNTERFACTUAL.example: If the platform had not retired, PAIR-001 would have been completed.
COUNTERFACTUAL.promotion_notes: Counterfactuals may not be promoted to OBSERVED or DERIVED without new conditions.

PROPOSED.definition: The proposition is put forward for consideration but has not been authorized or executed.
PROPOSED.promotion_notes: Proposals require explicit authorization before promotion to OBSERVED or DERIVED.

UNRESOLVED.definition: The proposition's epistemic status cannot be determined with currently available evidence.
UNRESOLVED.example: Whether the 106 unattempted units receive terminal dispositions due to retirement is UNRESOLVED.
UNRESOLVED.promotion_notes: Resolution requires new evidence or explicit protocol authorization, not assertion.

ordering_note: These statuses are NOT quality rankings. OBSERVED is not 'better' than HYPOTHESIZED; they carry different epistemic commitments. Do not use status as a proxy for confidence.

EPR_definition.description: Epistemic Promotion Rate. Tracks unlicensed strengthening of claim status across transitions.
EPR_definition.EPR_zero_requirement: Claims supporting primary conclusions require EPR = 0. An unlicensed promotion is not repaired by subsequent correction; the event and its disposition must remain in the record.
EPR_definition.unlicensed_promotion_definition: A promotion is unlicensed if: (a) a claim changes to a stronger status; and (b) no explicit transformation rule, new evidence binding, or authorization record justifies the change.

stronger_status_partial_order.description: For EPR purposes, the following partial order applies. A promotion is 'stronger' if it moves in the direction indicated.
stronger_status_partial_order.order: UNRESOLVED < PROPOSED < HYPOTHESIZED < COUNTERFACTUAL < DERIVED < OBSERVED
notes: This order is used only for EPR detection, not for evaluating claim quality.
COUNTERFACTUAL to OBSERVED is always unlicensed without new observational evidence.
HYPOTHESIZED to DERIVED requires an explicit transformation rule binding.

protocol_rules: Every material claim must have an explicitly assigned status in the ledger.
Status omission is a protocol violation.
An unlicensed promotion discovered post-hoc must be preserved with its disposition, not silently corrected.
Claim status may be revised downward (weakened) if new evidence requires it, without EPR penalty, provided the revision is documented.
